messages:
maya: Heads-up: I'm starting a canary rollout for the new rate-limit policy (reduce burst window from 60s->30s) targeting beta orgs. Will watch 5m windows.
liam: 👍 which metric dashboards should we watch first?
maya: watch `ingress.429_rate` and `edge.latency.p95` in the rate-limits dashboard. Also keep an eye on `auth.failures` in case token parsing hits a new path.
jon: tagging deploy-bot to confirm envs. @deploy-bot, which clusters will see the canary?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated: groups=[beta-west,beta-east], percentage=5%, policy=ratewindow-30s-v2, started_by=maya
sophia: FYI Customer support already has two threads open from a mobile-heavy customer complaining about intermittent 429s this morning. Amanda, can you coordinate if those customers are in beta groups?
amanda-cs: On it. Customer IDs C-431 and C-788 look like they are in beta-east. I'm pausing manual escalations until we have initial telemetery.
liam: Quick sanity check — the rollout config in s3 has the old TTL? snippet: ```yaml
policy: ratewindow-30s-v2
buckets: default=100
burst_window_sec: 30
apply_groups: ["beta-west","beta-east"]
```
maya: yep that's the one. Also enabling verbose logging for rate-limiter for canary groups: `rl.debug=true`
jon: If 429 spike happens, what's the rollback trigger threshold? Do we have an automated stop?
sophia: We set a soft stop: if cluster 429 rate > 3x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m buckets OR any customer-impacting P0 reports, abort canary. Manual rollback window 10m.
liam: I'll wire a temporary alert: `alert.ratepolicy.canary.429` -> paging on call if >3x baseline for 3m.
amanda-cs: I'm messaging the two affected customers with a heads-up and will collect repro (timestamps, client versions, sample request IDs).
maya: telemetry coming in: beta-east 429 count doubled in first min, but p95 latency unchanged. Looks like token parse errors in the logs: ```ERROR auth: token_parse_failed uid=C-431 err="malformed header"```
jon: That suggests malformed tokens surfaced by stricter windowing -> possibly burst smoothing in client. Might be retries amplifying 429s. Can we toggle smoothing fallback?
maya: ops-bot, enable fallback-route for beta-east to `legacy-window` if 429 spike detected.
ops-bot: Fallback rule applied for beta-east: route->legacy-window, reason=canary-safety, applied_by=maya
sophia: Good. That should prevent further customer impact while we investigate client-side retry behavior. Amanda, keep customers updated.
amanda-cs: will do. Asking for request IDs now.
liam: After fallback, 429s dropped back to baseline. Recommend we halt rollout, collect request traces, and run a small lab repro with aggressive retry clients.
maya: Agreed. Rolling back canary globally for beta groups now and opening an incident for root cause. jon, can you file the incident with steps and include the logs/output?
jon: Filing now: Incident INC-214159 — "canary ratewindow-30s-v2 causing token_parse 429s". Adding action items: repro, client retry pattern, rollout validation checklist.
sophia: Action items: 1) Repro in lab with C-431 request patterns, 2) Validate token parsing path under burst, 3) Add synthetic test for retry amplification, 4) Update canary checklist to include auth token schema check.
maya: Thanks all. Postmortem will include specific rollback thresholds and a customer communication draft. Amanda — can you draft a short note to affected customers offering a temporary workaround (disable aggressive client retries for 60s) and status update?
amanda-cs: Drafting now, will share in #customer-comm before sending. :thumbsup:
maya: Closing loop: rollback completed at 2141591890, incident created, customers notified in progress. Will follow up with lab repro results before reattempting any ratepolicy change.
